text: I'm reviewing three papers for CHI this cycle and every time I end up with the PDF in one window, the PCS form in another and a notes doc in a third, copying sentences back and forth. Can you make me one page with the paper on the left and my review on the right? Put in a made-up paper for now so I can try it (something accessibility-ish, a study with ~14 participants, a few sections and figure captions), I'll paste the real text in later. The form needs what the venue asks for: overall recommendation on their 1-5 scale (1 = I'd argue to reject, 3 = could go either way, 5 = I'd argue to accept), my expertise 1-4 (no knowledge / passing / knowledgeable / expert), and I like to rate originality, significance, rigour and clarity separately with one sentence each so my score is defensible. Then the review text itself with a word count. Most important bit: when I select a sentence in the paper I want to drop it into the review as a quote, so I'm responding to what they actually wrote and not my memory of it.
quoting works but it always lands at the bottom of the review. put it where my cursor is. and add the section number after the quote so I can write 'in 4.3 you say...' without scrolling back to check

add the reviewer checklist from the guidelines: anonymised properly, ethics/consent described, participants described (who, how many, how recruited, paid?), figures have alt text or are described, limitations discussed, contribution type stated, materials shared or a reason given. And somewhere at the bottom that tells me what I havent done yet before I paste it into PCS
the word count is counting the quotes too. I set myself 500 words of my own per review (ACs complain about short reviews), so show my words and quoted words separately and how far off 500 I am

ugh closed the tab by accident and lost an hour of writing. save as I type, localStorage is fine its just my laptop, and show when it last saved. also a copy button that gives me plain text in the order the PCS form wants: recommendation, expertise, the review, then the four criteria with my notes. a .txt download too in case clipboard is blocked
last thing: highlight the bits of the paper I've already quoted so I can see which parts my review actually covers. if I delete a quote from the review the highlight should go too
